title: Brute Force / Failed Login Spike SOP
source_excerpt: For a failed-login spike, verify account, source IP distribution, time window, and any successful login after repeated failures before escalation.
citation: COE Sample Auth Investigation SOP v1.0 AUTH-001
positive_examples: show users with failed login spike
brute force against admin
faild logins by user
answer_constraints: Do not declare compromise from failed-login counts alone.
Require approved evidence before severity or root-cause conclusions.
recommended_actions: Review failed-login volume and source distribution.
Check for successful login after repeated failures.
Escalate when privileged accounts or broad source spread are involved.

title: Failed Logins by Source IP SOP
source_excerpt: When failures cluster by source IP, compare unique users, geo or network ownership, and whether the source is expected for the environment.
citation: COE Sample Auth Investigation SOP v1.0 AUTH-002
positive_examples: top source IPs for failed logins
failed logins by src
answer_constraints: Treat source-IP reputation as contextual unless approved threat intel is available.
recommended_actions: Group failures by src and user.
Check whether source IP is expected or previously observed.

title: Successful Login After Repeated Failures Guidance
source_excerpt: A successful login following repeated failures should be reviewed for account criticality, source novelty, and session activity before escalation.
citation: COE Sample Auth Investigation SOP v1.0 AUTH-003
positive_examples: successful login after repeated failures
success following failed logins
answer_constraints: Do not call the account compromised without post-login evidence or approval.
recommended_actions: Correlate failure and success events for same user and src.
Check if source is new for the user.

title: Account Lockout Guidance
source_excerpt: Account lockout events should be checked for affected user criticality, repeated source patterns, and business-impact context.
citation: COE Sample Auth Investigation SOP v1.0 AUTH-004
positive_examples: account lockout after failed logins
answer_constraints: Do not infer malicious activity from a lockout without supporting source or timing evidence.
recommended_actions: Check lockout frequency and impacted user role.

title: New Source IP Login Guidance
source_excerpt: A login from a new source IP should be compared with prior user activity and expected access patterns before escalation.
citation: COE Sample Auth Investigation SOP v1.0 AUTH-005
positive_examples: new source IP login for user
first seen login source
answer_constraints: Do not label a new source as malicious without corroborating evidence.
recommended_actions: Compare source IP against user baseline.
Check whether VPN or jump host behavior is expected.

title: Splunk Auth Context Note
source_excerpt: COE sample auth searches use index=pgcil_soc and sourcetype=pgcil:auth with user, src, action, result, and _time fields.
citation: COE Sample Splunk Auth Context v1.0 SPLUNK-AUTH-001
positive_examples: generate SPL for failed logins
which sourcetype for auth failures
answer_constraints: Only use configured allowed indexes and sourcetypes during SPL validation.
prohibited_conclusions: all customer auth data is covered
recommended_actions: Validate generated SPL against deterministic SPL policy.

title: MITRE T1110 Reference Note
source_excerpt: T1110 is the Enterprise technique commonly used for brute-force password guessing and password spraying style behavior.
citation: COE Sample MITRE Auth Grounding v1.0 T1110
positive_examples: map brute force to MITRE
T1110 failed logins
answer_constraints: Use as grounding, not a final attack determination.
recommended_actions: Correlate with failed authentication evidence before final mapping.

title: MITRE T1078 Reference Note
source_excerpt: T1078 is the Enterprise technique commonly used for valid-account access, including suspicious successful authentication after failures.
citation: COE Sample MITRE Auth Grounding v1.0 T1078
positive_examples: successful login after failures T1078
new source IP valid account
answer_constraints: Use as grounding, not a final attack determination.
recommended_actions: Correlate successful auth with user baseline before final mapping.

title: Escalation Guidance for HIL
source_excerpt: Escalate auth scenarios to a tier2 SOC analyst when privileged accounts, success-after-failure, or broad source distribution are present.
citation: COE Sample Auth Escalation Matrix v1.0 ESC-AUTH-001
positive_examples: requires human review for brute force
escalate successful login after failures
when should repeated failed login alerts be assigned to L2
answer_constraints: Escalation guidance is advisory and does not authorize execution.
recommended_actions: Review the validated SPL and collection status before approving mock execution.
Request more evidence if source coverage is insufficient.

tool selection for spl_search
answer_constraints: LLMs must not call MCP directly.
prohibited_conclusions: LLM may select arbitrary MCP tools
recommended_actions: Keep deterministic MCP selector authoritative.

title: Auth Failed Login SPL Pattern Note
source_excerpt: For governed SPL generation, aggregate authentication failures over a bounded time window and group by user and source fields before analyst review.
citation: COE Sample Auth Detection Engineering Note v1.0 DET-AUTH-001
positive_examples: generate SPL for failed login aggregation
SPL failed auth by user and src
answer_constraints: Generated SPL must remain candidate-only until deterministic validation approves it.
recommended_actions: Use bounded time windows.
Aggregate before presenting candidate SPL.

title: Analyst checklist: auth after hours critical asset
source_excerpt: Confirm user, host, source IP, and event time. Compare against the user's normal working hours and asset criticality. Check for concurrent failures or new-source logins. Validate before severity claims.
positive_examples: Confirm user, host, source IP, and event time.

title: Investigation workflow: auth after hours critical asset
source_excerpt: Scope after-hours authentications to critical assets by user/host/time. Compare against baseline working hours and known maintenance windows. Pivot to source reputation and concurrent activity. Keep SPL generation and execution behind validation and review gates.
positive_examples: Scope after-hours authentications to critical assets by user/host/time.

title: Limitations and non-claims: auth after hours critical asset
source_excerpt: Off-hours activity is common for shift workers, automation, and global teams. Timing alone does not establish valid-account abuse.
positive_examples: Off-hours activity is common for shift workers, automation, and global teams.

title: Answer rules: auth after hours critical asset
source_excerpt: Do not claim compromise from after-hours timing alone. Valid-account abuse (T1078) is candidate-only without corroborating anomaly or context. Do not assert credential dumping (T1003) from login timing. SPL/execution remains review-gated.
positive_examples: Do not claim compromise from after-hours timing alone.

title: Analyst checklist: auth failed login spike
source_excerpt: Validate time window and threshold. Compare distinct users and sources. Check whether any successful authentication followed the failures. Review asset or account criticality before severity claims.
positive_examples: Validate time window and threshold.

title: Investigation workflow: auth failed login spike
source_excerpt: Scope authentication failures by user, source, host, and time window. Confirm threshold evidence before labeling brute-force activity evidence-supported. Pivot to success-after-failure only when successful authentication evidence exists. Keep SPL generation and execution behind existing validation and review gates.
positive_examples: Scope authentication failures by user, source, host, and time window.

title: Limitations and non-claims: auth failed login spike
source_excerpt: Failed login telemetry alone does not establish credential validity. Source IP reuse, NAT, or scanner behavior may require analyst review.
positive_examples: Failed login telemetry alone does not establish credential validity.

title: Answer rules: auth failed login spike
source_excerpt: Do not claim account compromise from failed logins alone. Mark brute force as evidence-supported only after threshold evidence exists. SPL/execution remains review-gated.
positive_examples: Do not claim account compromise from failed logins alone.

title: Analyst checklist: auth privileged login anomaly
source_excerpt: Confirm whether the login matches the user's normal access pattern, shift timing, location, and device. Check whether the account is privileged, dormant, service-like, or recently modified. Check whether the target asset is crown-jewel, domain controller, OT engineering workstation, or SCADA gateway. Review failure-then-success ordering and whether multiple users authenticated from the same source IP. Review the MFA outcome and whether the source IP is new for this user. Review first post-login commands, remote service use, and access to sensitive shares or credential stores. Escalate to the IT/OT incident bridge when the target is OT or crown-jewel infrastructure.
positive_examples: Confirm whether the login matches the user's normal access pattern, shift timing, location, and device.

title: Investigation workflow: auth privileged login anomaly
source_excerpt: Scope and baseline: identify source and destination (workstation, jump server, VPN gateway, PAW, OT host, cloud console); confirm the login matches the user's normal pattern, shift, location, and device. Account and asset context: check whether the account is privileged, dormant, service-like, or recently modified; check whether the target is crown-jewel, domain controller, OT engineering workstation, or SCADA gateway. Authentication evidence: check repeated failures before success for the same user/source/host/time window; check multiple users from one source IP; review MFA outcome (approved, denied, timeout, push fatigue, bypass, none); validate source IP novelty against known corporate or VPN egress. Post-authentication pivots: review first commands, processes, or administrative actions after login; check for PsExec, WMI, PowerShell remoting, RDP, SMB admin shares, or unusual remote s
positive_examples: Scope and baseline: identify source and destination (workstation, jump server, VPN gateway, PAW, OT host, cloud console); confirm the login matches the user's normal pattern, shift, location, and devi

title: Limitations and non-claims: auth privileged login anomaly
source_excerpt: A single anomalous admin login does not confirm compromise. Login metadata alone cannot support evidence-supported MITRE claims. High admin activity may be scheduled maintenance, automation, or approved support activity. No containment or account action may be performed without HIL/change approval.
positive_examples: A single anomalous admin login does not confirm compromise.

title: Answer rules: auth privileged login anomaly
source_excerpt: State that this checklist validates whether an admin login is expected, suspicious, or requires escalation; it does not confirm compromise by itself. Keep T1078 Valid Accounts as a candidate when the login is suspicious but not proven malicious. Mention T1110 brute force only when the failure pattern supports it. Mention post-login techniques (remote services, PowerShell, credential access, collection) only when observed evidence supports them. MITRE mappings remain candidates until supported by source-grounded evidence.
positive_examples: State that this checklist validates whether an admin login is expected, suspicious, or requires escalation; it does not confirm compromise by itself.

title: Analyst checklist: auth success after failure
source_excerpt: Confirm failure and success event ordering. Review whether the source is known for the user. Check privileged account or critical asset context. Look for follow-on activity before compromise language.
positive_examples: Confirm failure and success event ordering.

title: Investigation workflow: auth success after failure
source_excerpt: Correlate failures followed by successful authentication for the same user, source, host, and time window. Check source IP novelty where available. Keep Valid Accounts as a candidate unless additional misuse evidence exists.
positive_examples: Correlate failures followed by successful authentication for the same user, source, host, and time window.

title: Limitations and non-claims: auth success after failure
source_excerpt: Sequence evidence can be benign if the user retried successfully. Novelty is optional and may be unavailable in current telemetry.
positive_examples: Sequence evidence can be benign if the user retried successfully.

title: Answer rules: auth success after failure
source_excerpt: State 'successful login after failures observed.' Do not state 'compromised account' unless additional evidence exists. T1078 remains candidate unless stronger account-misuse evidence exists.
positive_examples: State 'successful login after failures observed.'

title: Analyst checklist: critical notable mitre review
source_excerpt: Confirm the critical alerts, affected hosts, and time window. Map observed behavior to MITRE ATT&CK candidates (not confirmed). Check vulnerability-source onboarding status; correlate CVEs only with asset + CPE join keys. Validate asset criticality before severity claims.
positive_examples: Confirm the critical alerts, affected hosts, and time window.

title: Investigation workflow: critical notable mitre review
source_excerpt: Scope critical/notable alerts by host and time window. Derive candidate MITRE techniques from alert behavior. Attach CVE context from the onboarded snapshot when asset + product join keys are present; otherwise mark advisory. Keep SPL generation and execution behind validation and review gates.
positive_examples: Scope critical/notable alerts by host and time window.

title: Limitations and non-claims: critical notable mitre review
source_excerpt: MITRE mappings are candidate-tier without corroborating evidence. CVE correlation requires asset inventory + product/CPE join keys; snapshot presence alone is not a host-level unpatched-CVE claim.
positive_examples: MITRE mappings are candidate-tier without corroborating evidence.

title: Answer rules: critical notable mitre review
source_excerpt: Correlate critical alerts with MITRE ATT&CK at candidate tier; do not assert confirmed techniques without supporting evidence. CVE correlation is advisory: state vulnerability-source status, and require asset + product/CPE join keys before any 'unpatched CVE on affected host' claim. Do not claim credential dumping (T1003) or defense impairment (T1562.001) without direct evidence. SPL/execution remains review-gated.
positive_examples: Correlate critical alerts with MITRE ATT&CK at candidate tier; do not assert confirmed techniques without supporting evidence.

title: Analyst checklist: dns beaconing candidate
source_excerpt: Measure periodicity and jitter. Check bytes out and DNS query count. Assess domain rarity and destination context. Tie traffic to a host or user before impact language.
positive_examples: Measure periodicity and jitter.

title: Investigation workflow: dns beaconing candidate
source_excerpt: Review periodicity, jitter, outbound volume, and domain rarity together. Associate source with user or host identity when possible. Escalate from candidate to evidence-supported only when multiple signals align.
positive_examples: Review periodicity, jitter, outbound volume, and domain rarity together.

title: Limitations and non-claims: dns beaconing candidate
source_excerpt: Periodic traffic may be benign polling or monitoring. Parent T1071 is used unless evidence supports a specific sub-technique.
positive_examples: Periodic traffic may be benign polling or monitoring.

title: Answer rules: dns beaconing candidate
source_excerpt: Do not claim C2 confirmed from periodicity alone. Use candidate/evidence-supported wording based on multiple signals.
positive_examples: Do not claim C2 confirmed from periodicity alone.

title: Analyst checklist: edr powershell suspicious command
source_excerpt: Review event ID and script block text. Check parent process and user context. Identify encoded-command usage. Look for related network connections or child processes.
positive_examples: Review event ID and script block text.

title: Investigation workflow: edr powershell suspicious command
source_excerpt: Collect process, command line, parent process, and script block evidence. Flag encoded command or suspicious invocation patterns as evidence, not malware verdicts. Pivot to network and child-process activity when available.
positive_examples: Collect process, command line, parent process, and script block evidence.

title: Limitations and non-claims: edr powershell suspicious command
source_excerpt: Administrative scripts may use PowerShell legitimately. Encoded command is a suspicious indicator, not a standalone malware verdict.
positive_examples: Administrative scripts may use PowerShell legitimately.

title: Answer rules: edr powershell suspicious command
source_excerpt: Do not classify as malware unless malware evidence exists. State suspicious command execution evidence and required pivots.
positive_examples: Do not classify as malware unless malware evidence exists.

title: Analyst checklist: edr suspicious process
source_excerpt: Confirm process_name, parent_process, and command_line. Check for encoded or download command-line markers. Review host/user criticality before severity claims. Corroborate with network or persistence signals.
positive_examples: Confirm process_name, parent_process, and command_line.

title: Investigation workflow: edr suspicious process
source_excerpt: Scope suspicious process executions by host, user, and time window. Identify LOLBins and encoded/download command lines. Pivot to parent/child lineage and network connections. Keep SPL generation and execution behind validation and review gates.
positive_examples: Scope suspicious process executions by host, user, and time window.

title: Limitations and non-claims: edr suspicious process
source_excerpt: Process execution telemetry alone does not establish malicious intent. Legitimate admin tooling can match LOLBin patterns.
positive_examples: Process execution telemetry alone does not establish malicious intent.

title: Answer rules: edr suspicious process
source_excerpt: Do not claim malware or compromise from process execution alone. LOLBin or encoded/download command lines are suspicious, not proof; mark execution evidence-supported only with corroborating telemetry. Do not assert Impair Defenses (T1562.001) without direct tool/service tamper evidence. SPL/execution remains review-gated.
positive_examples: Do not claim malware or compromise from process execution alone.

title: Analyst checklist: email phishing header review
source_excerpt: Check SPF, DKIM, and DMARC alignment. Review sender and reply-to mismatch. Collect URL/domain and attachment indicators. Confirm gateway verdict and affected recipients.
positive_examples: Check SPF, DKIM, and DMARC alignment.

title: Investigation workflow: email phishing header review
source_excerpt: Compare sender, return-path, reply-to, and authentication results. Inspect URL/domain, attachment, recipient, and gateway verdict evidence. Classify wording based on combined evidence strength.
positive_examples: Compare sender, return-path, reply-to, and authentication results.

title: Limitations and non-claims: email phishing header review
source_excerpt: Email header anomalies may reflect forwarding or gateway behavior. Phishing verdict needs more than a single mismatch signal.
positive_examples: Email header anomalies may reflect forwarding or gateway behavior.

title: Answer rules: email phishing header review
source_excerpt: Do not claim phishing confirmed only from sender mismatch. Distinguish suspicious, likely phishing, and evidence-supported phishing.
positive_examples: Do not claim phishing confirmed only from sender mismatch.

title: Analyst checklist: endpoint ransomware impact review
source_excerpt: Measure file rename count and extension patterns. Identify affected paths and process name. Check shadow copy deletion and service stop indicators. Count impacted hosts before scope claims.
positive_examples: Measure file rename count and extension patterns.

title: Investigation workflow: endpoint ransomware impact review
source_excerpt: Collect file-change, process, recovery-inhibition, service-stop, and host-impact signals. Use T1486 evidence-supported wording only when multiple impact signals align. Require human review for containment or remediation recommendations.
positive_examples: Collect file-change, process, recovery-inhibition, service-stop, and host-impact signals.

title: Limitations and non-claims: endpoint ransomware impact review
source_excerpt: Bulk file changes can be benign administrative or backup activity. This enrichment does not include malware reverse-engineering or decryptor guidance.
positive_examples: Bulk file changes can be benign administrative or backup activity.

title: Answer rules: endpoint ransomware impact review
source_excerpt: Do not claim ransomware from file changes alone. Require multiple evidence signals for evidence-supported T1486. Require HIL for containment or remediation guidance.
positive_examples: Do not claim ransomware from file changes alone.

title: Analyst checklist: net firewall deny spike
source_excerpt: Confirm src, dest, deny_count, and destination ports. Distinguish inbound scanning from outbound blocked traffic. Check destination reputation and port spread. Validate before severity claims.
positive_examples: Confirm src, dest, deny_count, and destination ports.

title: Investigation workflow: net firewall deny spike
source_excerpt: Scope firewall denies per source/destination with port spread and time window. Separate scanning/misconfig from targeted blocked activity. Pivot to reputation and correlated host telemetry. Keep SPL generation and execution behind validation and review gates.
positive_examples: Scope firewall denies per source/destination with port spread and time window.

title: Limitations and non-claims: net firewall deny spike
source_excerpt: Deny events represent blocked traffic; a spike is not evidence of successful compromise. Scanning and misconfiguration are common benign causes.
positive_examples: Deny events represent blocked traffic; a spike is not evidence of successful compromise.

title: Answer rules: net firewall deny spike
source_excerpt: Do not assert intrusion or C2 from a firewall deny spike alone. Deny spikes are frequently scanning, misconfiguration, or blocked-by-design traffic. No MITRE technique is asserted for deny-volume alone; keep mappings not-claimed without corroborating evidence. SPL/execution remains review-gated.
positive_examples: Do not assert intrusion or C2 from a firewall deny spike alone.

title: Analyst checklist: net vpn login anomaly
source_excerpt: Confirm user, source IPs, and failure counts. Distinguish single-user lockout from distributed source spread. Check for a successful VPN login following the failures. Validate before severity claims.
positive_examples: Confirm user, source IPs, and failure counts.

title: Investigation workflow: net vpn login anomaly
source_excerpt: Scope failed VPN authentications per user with source spread and time window. Separate credential/config issues from distributed guessing. Pivot to success-after-failure and source reputation. Keep SPL generation and execution behind validation and review gates.
positive_examples: Scope failed VPN authentications per user with source spread and time window.

title: Limitations and non-claims: net vpn login anomaly
source_excerpt: Failed VPN logins alone do not establish credential validity or compromise. NAT/shared egress can inflate source counts.
positive_examples: Failed VPN logins alone do not establish credential validity or compromise.

title: Answer rules: net vpn login anomaly
source_excerpt: Do not claim breach from a VPN failed-login spike alone. Spikes may be expired credentials, client misconfig, or MFA friction — not necessarily attack. Valid-account abuse (T1078) is candidate-only; needs success-after-anomaly + context. SPL/execution remains review-gated.
positive_examples: Do not claim breach from a VPN failed-login spike alone.

title: Analyst checklist: soc incident triage
source_excerpt: Confirm alert type and affected asset. Collect severity policy inputs. Review prior related alerts. Record containment state without recommending destructive action.
positive_examples: Confirm alert type and affected asset.

title: Investigation workflow: soc incident triage
source_excerpt: Summarize alert type, affected asset, user, status, related alerts, and containment state. Use SOP guidance without assigning MITRE absent alert evidence. Require human approval for containment or remediation.
positive_examples: Summarize alert type, affected asset, user, status, related alerts, and containment state.

title: Limitations and non-claims: soc incident triage
source_excerpt: Playbook guidance depends on alert evidence supplied by the analyst or governed retrieval. No remediation action is authorized by this enrichment.
positive_examples: Playbook guidance depends on alert evidence supplied by the analyst or governed retrieval.

title: Answer rules: soc incident triage
source_excerpt: Use IR/SOP guidance. Do not recommend destructive containment. Human approval required for containment/remediation. Do not assign MITRE without alert type/evidence.
positive_examples: Use IR/SOP guidance.
